Israelis have shot dead two teenagers in a Palestinian village encircled by settlers and Israeli troops have razed an entire village outside Hebron, the latest attacks in a surge of Israeli terror and ethnic cleansing across the occupied West Bank.

events.summary:
Air bases used by US in UAE and Kuwait hit as Israeli defence chief says Iran’s regime fears collapse due to economic pressures

Iran has continued to demonstrate an ability to target bases in the Gulf used by the US despite six months of war and a new sanctions regime described by the Trump administration as an “economic D-day”.

As Iran’s military targeted US bases in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, despite threats of further strikes by the US president, Israel’s defence chief warned that economic pressures from the sanctions could lead Tehran to escalate to more “extreme measures”.

events.summary:
Defence minister says he believes US backing could tip regional balance in favour of forced resettlement

Israel’s defence minister has said his country is seeking Donald Trump’s support to approve plans to expel Palestinians from the Gaza Strip in what has widely been condemned as a potential war crime.

Israel Katz said there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this
migration” during a conference hosted by the Israeli news site Ynet and the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth. He said the Israeli government was “organised and prepared to get them out by sea, by air, by every way possible”.

Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber.

Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.

events.summary:

Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India.

Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.

A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found.

Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38.

events.summary:

A British aid worker was mistakenly identified by Nepalese authorities as a rescued survivor after returning to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid flight.

Alastair Chambers, a 45-year-old former Gloucester councillor, said he flew to Nepal last week to distribute sleeping bags, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges.

Nepali rescuers have built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas to rescue hundreds of trapped workers, as the death toll passed 1,000 nearly ⁠a week after devastating ​floods left a trail of destruction across the country’s towns and valleys.

About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts. The prime ⁠minister, Balendra Shah, said more than 11,000 people had been rescued across the affected region, and power and communication lines had been restored in some areas.

British people have been urged to have enough food and water on hand to survive a few days without power or water, as the UN said the El Niño climate phenomenon was “supersizing before our eyes”, exacerbating extreme weather events worldwide.

Forecasters say they are braced for the biggest El Niño in 1,000 years, bringing wildfires and floods to parts of the world, and the threat of a wet, stormy winter for the UK.

As the British government plans a campaign urging citizens to prepare for national emergencies, Angela Eagle told the Guardian the likelihood of a wild winter showed the importance of having supplies at home.

England’s higher education regulator has apologised for a string of mistakes in its decision to punish the University of Sussex with a record fine that was later overturned by the high court.

The Office for Students (OfS) tried to impose a £585,000 fine against Sussex last year after claiming the university breached free speech regulations involving its former professor Kathleen Stock. It was forced to back down in April after a judicial review initiated by Sussex found the OfS “had closed its mind” and acted with bias.

events.summary:

Homeowners in the UK are braced for a jump in mortgage rates, driven by higher inflation and interest rate increase expectations amid turmoil in the global bond markets.

The former pardon attorney for the US justice department, Elizabeth Oyer, filed a lawsuit on Thursday against the department and attorney general Todd Blanche, accusing them of “unlawfully” firing her last year after she said she refused to recommend restoring actor Mel Gibson’s gun rights.

In the complaint, filed in the US district court for the District of Columbia, Oyer alleges that in early 2025, while she was serving as pardon attorney, she was asked to “disregard her duties and facilitate a political favor” for Gibson based on his “relationship with President Trump”.

Leading figures from politics, entertainment and wider society led glowing tributes to Gloria Steinem on Thursday, with Hillary Clinton hailing the American feminist icon who died at 92 at home in New York City as “one of the architects of the entire structure of women’s equality”.

events.title: Why social media addiction is so hard to regulate
events.summary: Facebook, Instagram and other social media platforms are accused of deliberately fostering addictive behavior among young users. Yet regulators continue to struggle to rein in their engagement-driven business models.

events.title: CDU's Volkmann: Ukraine aid is not charity
events.summary: Former German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's grandson Johannes Volkmann spoke to DW about why Germany must continue to support Ukraine.

events.title: Bundesliga season 2026-27: All you need to know
events.summary: From key dates to rising football stars and changes, DW has the latest on the new Bundesliga season.

events.title: Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama dies at 97
events.summary: From works of "self-obliteration" to polka dotted nudes, the pioneering artist developed a unique body of work likely to be relevant for years to come.

events.title: Was the heat of this summer really 'normal?'
events.summary: Some political messaging denies the role of human-caused climate change in this summer's extreme heat. The science tells a different story.

events.title: Tim Curry, of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' dies at 80
events.summary: The gender-bending role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter put Curry on the map in 1975. He then went on to play a number of villainous roles like Gomez Addams, Pennywise and Bill Sikes, but also Mozart and William Shakespeare.

events.title: Reports: UEFA backs off FIFA boycott threat
events.summary: UEFA is reportedly set to withdraw a threat to boycott FIFA tournaments over a plan to partially privatize football tournaments. The Under-20 Women's World Cup is to be hosted by Poland next month.

events.title: Gamescom 2026: What's next for the gaming industry?
events.summary: As Gamescom 2026 opens in Cologne, AI, hardware costs and slowing user growth are putting pressure on the global games industry despite its current strength.

events.title: Remembering Dolly Parton: 8 facts about the icon
events.summary: Dolly Parton, one of the world's most successful artists, has died at the age of 80. Here are some important and extraordinary facts about the country music superstar.

events.title: US country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80
events.summary: Representatives of the country music legend told US media that Dolly Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer." Parton's career spans more than half a century and includes a wide array of smash hits.

events.title: Grain exports stall as Ukraine steps up attacks on Russia's Black Sea ports
events.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian infrastructure on the Black Sea are disrupting grain and oil exports from the port of Novorossiysk and other key hubs.

events.title: Schalke coach looks to Bosnia bond in Bundesliga return
events.summary: After three seasons in the second division, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga. Just a year ago, few would have guessed that their revival would largely be 'Made in Bosnia.'

events.title: Can Germany defend itself against drone attacks?
events.summary: Explosive-laden drones at Leipzig/Halle airport have exposed gaps in Germany's defenses. DW looks at how prepared the country is for future drone attacks.

events.title: Why Germany's Volkswagen could cut 100,000 jobs
events.summary: Europe's biggest automaker, Volkswagen, faces Chinese competition, high costs and US tariffs. What could its restructuring mean for the German car industry?

events.title: Can new US sanctions cripple Iran's shadow economy?
events.summary: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.

events.title: Trees are vital for cooler cities, but they need help too
events.summary: Record-breaking heat and drought are putting urban trees at risk. Experts explain how to protect these essential assets and build city forests that can withstand the climate challenges ahead.

events.title: The new Bundesliga season is here, but has the glow gone?
events.summary: Another Bundesliga season arrives, but are the golden years of Germany's top football league already over, and what can it do to change its course?

events.title: Star violinist Anne-Sophie Mutter: 50 years on stage
events.summary: Anne-Sophie Mutter constantly reinvents herself. For her 50th onstage anniversary, the star violinist is surprising audiences with sounds from around the world and never-before-recorded commissions.

events.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
events.summary: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

events.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
events.summary: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

events.title: Could Russia's growing fuel crisis help end the Ukraine war?
events.summary: Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries have deepened Russia's fuel crisis, with shortages reaching Moscow. Could growing public anger put Putin under pressure?

events.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections
events.summary: The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.

events.title: What is the 'political firewall' against Germany's far-right AfD?
events.summary: Germany's centrist parties reject any cooperation with the Alternative for Germany (AfD), parts of which are classified as right-wing extremist. However, this policy is coming under increasing pressure.

events.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
events.summary: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

events.title: Could Ukraine's Mykhailo Fedorov challenge Zelenskyy?
events.summary: An explosive video released last week by Ukraine's former defense minister spoke of corruption, a crisis of leadership and elections. What could follow?

events.title: Industry and residents clash over water near Berlin
events.summary: The state surrounding Berlin is drying out, but local Tesla and Red Bull plants are looking to expand. Is Brandenburg running out of water to share?

events.title: Germany investigates arms cache found in woods near Berlin
events.summary: Handguns and ammunition were found in a forest near Berlin last year. Reports say German authorities suspect they were to be used for assassinations on behalf of Russian intelligence.

events.title: 'Masha and the Bear': Ukraine sanctions Russian cartoon
events.summary: Ukraine has imposed sanctions on the hit Russian children's cartoon "Masha and the Bear," a step towards banning it. The culture minister called the show propaganda. Russia said the move showed Kyiv's "ugly nature."

events.title: What to do when wildfires trigger trauma
events.summary: The wildfires this summer have broken records in Germany and are unlikely to subside in future. Psychologists say post-traumatic stress disorder caused by such disasters is serious but can be treated if people seek help.

events.title: Bauhaus Manifesto: Broad alliance promoting artistic freedom
events.summary: Weeks before Saxony-Anhalt's state election, representatives from German cultural, crafts, architecture, design and church sectors unite to promote freedom, openness and creativity.

events.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
events.summary: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier.

events.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
events.summary: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.

events.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
events.summary: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.

events.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern Munich
events.summary: Bernadette Amani is heading into her first full season with Bayern Munich, having joined the club in January. Making a living at football is something she never imagined possible while growing up in rural Ivory Coast.

events.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
events.summary: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala collapses on pitch again
events.summary: One of Germany's top footballers has collapsed on the pitch for a second time in four days ahead of the new season. Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala has said he has a "neurological dysfunction" that causes blackouts.

events.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
events.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

events.title: Messi retirement hint highlights football era nearing an end
events.summary: Soon after propelling Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, Lionel Messi has cast some doubt on his future. While retirement doesn't seem imminent, it still beckons for him and Cristiano Ronaldo.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
events.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

events.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
events.summary: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

events.title: Dressed for power: Giorgia Meloni and the language of fashion
events.summary: From Giorgia Meloni's shift from dark suits to pastels to Angela Merkel's signature jackets, politicians have long used clothing to shape how voters see them. In this day and age, power dressing has evolved.

events.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
events.summary: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

events.title: How Germany's Hyrox became a global fitness craze
events.summary: Created in Germany and now a global success, Hyrox combines running and functional training into a unique format. How a German concept became an international sports phenomenon.

events.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
events.summary: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.

events.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble
events.summary: The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?

events.title: Can the cool north handle a surge in climate tourism?
events.summary: With heat records continually being broken and southern summers getting hotter, travelers are heading north. Fragile ecosystems are paying the price.

events.title: Fatty food raises risk of colorectal cancer
events.summary: Did you know fatty foods can increase production of an acid in your gut that promotes tumor growth? That's on top of all the other health risks linked to fatty foods, like fries and burgers.

events.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
events.summary: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.

events.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
events.summary: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

events.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
events.summary: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.

events.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?
events.summary: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

events.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
events.summary: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

events.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
events.summary: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
events.summary: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.

events.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
events.summary: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
events.summary: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
events.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

events.title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
events.summary: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

events.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
events.summary: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.

events.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
events.summary: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.

events.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
events.summary: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.

events.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
events.summary: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

events.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
events.summary: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

events.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
events.summary: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

events.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
events.summary: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.

events.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
events.summary: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
events.summary: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.

events.title: The hidden problem with small modular nuclear reactors
events.summary: Mini nuclear reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep
events.summary: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.

events.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
events.summary: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.

events.title: ‘Fight through darkness, water’: Nepal survivor recounts escape from flood-hit tunnel
events.summary: A Nepalese worker recounts his harrowing escape from a hydropower project tunnel after last week's devastating flood. Around 900 workers remain trapped in tunnels at six hydroelectric plants in Nepal as the number of missing in the Himalayan disaster rose to 5,624 on Thursday, according to Nepalese and Chinese authorities.

events.title: Anti-Christian murder in Syria? No indication he was killed because of his faith
events.summary: A Christian man by the name of Nader Boulos Tannous was murdered in Homs, Syria on August 15, 2026. After his death, Israel, Greece and Cyprus were quick to denounce what they called an anti-Christian act. Several days later however, authorities in Homs said the suspect had admitted killing Tannous as part of a personal dispute going back to 2012.

events.title: WMO chief says El Nino could be strongest in four decades
events.summary: El Nino could be the strongest since records began four decades ago, the United Nations' climate agency warned Thursday, with the UN chief warning the world is in the "danger zone of extreme weather". The naturally-occurring weather phenomenon is set to become "very strong" in the months ahead and is near certain to persist through to February, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said. FRANCE 24's Journalist Carys Garland tells us more.

events.title: Two Palestinian teens killed in West Bank raid by Israeli settlers and army
events.summary: Two Palestinian teenagers ⁠were killed on ​Wednesday in an attack by Israeli settler militants and ​army troops on their village in the occupied West Bank, local officials and the Palestinian health ministry said, amid an uptick in violence ​by ‌Jewish settlers in the territory. The Israeli military said in a statement its forces had entered al-Mughayyir to ​provide security for police officers and an Israeli ‌civilian seeking to retrieve livestock.

events.title: US energy firms dominate Venezuela deals worth billions
events.summary: US energy firms on Wednesday signed a raft of multi-billion-dollar deals with Venezuela, days after the South American country agreed to grant the United States control of a huge chunk of its vast oil reserves. President Donald Trump has talked up the agreement on Venezuela's oil reserves as the "biggest oil deal in world history." But the deals have raised major questions about Venezuela's sovereignty, as FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

events.title: France agriculture production sees economic hit from heatwaves
events.summary: France's recent heatwaves didn't just pose enormous health risks, they also hampered the economy. Authorities have estimated that the recent heat and drought caused production to plummet and expect wealth generated by the agricultural sector to decline by 8% over the course of the year. The knock-on effects will cost the French economy an estimated 0.1 percentage points of growth in 2026.

events.title: US feminist icon and journalist Gloria Steinem dies aged 92
events.summary: The co-founder of Ms. Magazine and celebrated feminist icon Gloria Steinem has died at her home at the age of 92. An internationally recognised activist in the fight for women's equality, she spoke out for the legalisation of abortion, same-sex marriage, and equal pay. She began her journalism career in New York in the 1960s. Politically, she was an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, arguing that the US had taken many steps back when it came to women's rights. FRANCE 24's Journalist and host of "The 51%" tells us more.

events.title: Why Ukraine’s drained Kakhovka Dam is strategic for Russia
events.summary: Small groups of Russian soldiers have been inching forward through the vast, drained Kakhovka reservoir since they blew up the dam in June 2023. Russian forces are infiltrating this “no man’s land” for reconnaissance purposes rather than for a future military offensive, said a military expert.

events.title: Giorgia Meloni government becomes Italy's longest-lasting since World War II
events.summary: Italy's first female Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, has surpassed a longevity record set by the late Silvio Berlusconi. When she took office in 2022, many European allies viewed her with unease, given her party's neo-fascist roots. Yet she has governed pragmatically, working within EU institutions and even supporting Ukraine. Domestically, however, she has targeted same-sex parents and clamped down on press freedom.

events.title: France-UK ties and humour celebrated as London receives Bayeux Tapestry
events.summary: French President Emmanuel #Macron is in #London on the occasion of the #Bayeux Tapestry's exhibition at the #BritishMuseum. The 1,000-year-old work of woven art recounts the Battle of #Hastings, in which William the Conqueror – #KingCharles's ancestor – led the Norman Conquest of #England. An opportunity for the French president, the British PM Andy #Burnham and British monarch to celebrate the strong ties between the two countries.

events.title: Driverless robotaxis hit the streets of London
events.summary: London is entering the era of autonomous vehicles: driverless cabs are now available through Uber and British tech firm Wayve in the capital. It marks a setback for Google's Waymo and Chinese giant Baidu, which have been eyeing Europe as a largely untapped market for autonomous vehicles. But for Wayve, it is its first mass-market rollout, and the company now plans to expand to Tokyo and 10 other cities with Uber.

events.title: Murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia: Campaigner 'devastated' at tycoon's acquittal
events.summary: A campaigner who has worked on the case of murdered Maltese journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia since she was killed by a car bomb in 2017 has spoken of his devastation at the not guilty verdict.

events.title: Spanish PM Sanchez says no evidence Morocco orchestrated Ceuta border surge
events.summary: Spain has found no evidence to conclude that July's deadly border rush from Morocco into its enclave of Ceuta was orchestrated by Moroccan authorities, ​Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez ‌said on Thursday, countering allegations in a Spanish police report. Speaking in parliament, Sanchez responded to claims in ⁠the report that emerged this week suggesting the entry of over 70,000 people into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration but a planned effort to overwhelm  border controls.

events.title: Outrage mounts in Malta after acquittal over journalist's murder
events.summary: Hundreds of people demonstrated in the Maltese capital Valletta after a wealthy businessman was found not guilty of masterminding the murder of an investigative journalist. The verdict on Daphne Caruana Galizia's car-bomb killing in 2017 sparked outrage from Maltese civil society groups and international media freedom organisations. The opposition Nationalist Party, which organised the demonstration late on Wednesday, has said lawmakers should be called back from their summer break for a special session of the legislature to discuss the case.

events.title: Beastie Boy Mike D releases his first solo LP 'Thank You'
events.summary: Mike D rose to fame in the 1980s as part of New York's Beastie Boys, a rap-rock trio who soon tired of poking fun at frat boy humour with hits like "Fight for Your Right (To Party!)" and" Girls". The band quickly moved on thanks to their passion for beat making, sampling and playing around in the studio, establishing themselves over three decades as credible genre-bending musicians.

events.title: 'Glacier melt and sea level rise will continue:  We cannot leave this to the next generation'
events.summary: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Inger Andersen, Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations and Executive Director of the United Nations Environment Programme. Her central argument is that decades of what she calls “carbon procrastination” have made exceeding 1.5°C unavoidable: the question is therefore no longer simply whether the world crosses 1.5°C, but by how much, for how long, and with what consequences for vulnerable societies and ecosystems. While mitigation remains essential, adaptation becomes equally important as sea-level rise and glacier loss, will continue even as emissions fall.

events.title: Nepal Floods: Survivors hauled to safety with makeshift zip line
events.summary: Nepali authorities have erected a makeshift zip line to help stranded residents travel across the swollen waters of the Trishuli river after last week’s deadly flash floods swept away bridges, leaving them cut off from the outside world. Some were in need of urgent treatment, medicines, food and other essentials.

events.title: Please welcome the newest member to our team: The AI agent
events.summary: This week, we're looking look at efforts to incorporate artificial intelligence into the workplace. But not just your run-of-the-mill generative AI chatbot: we're focusing on actual AI agents. These are autonomous programs designed to take on tasks and work through a series of steps without the user having to specify every move. And they're moving into our everyday lives – helping people plan holidays, shop online and take care of other routine tasks.

events.title: A 'Lille' bit of everything at Europe's biggest flea market
events.summary: Every year, millions of people flock to the French city of Lille on the first weekend of September for Europe's biggest flea market, the "Braderie de Lille". We dive into its rich history, the many terms for second-hand shopping in French, plus the delicious tradition that's now synonymous with this 34-hour event: mussels and fries!

events.title: Tunisia water crisis deepens as temperatures approach 50°C
events.summary: In Tunisia, powerful heatwaves are driving power cuts and water shortage. While the country has been dealing with structural water scarcity and recurring drought for years, the current crisis is fuelling anger against the government, even as authorities attempt to coordinate water distribution efforts to quell the crisis.

events.title: France's Macron meets UK PM Burnham at Downing Street
events.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron met Britain’s new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, for official talks at 10 Downing Street. The meeting came a day after the pair were joined by King Charles and Queen Camilla at the British Museum for a preview of the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London. Macron is the first EU leader to meet Burnham. Talks are expected to cover relations between Britain and the European Union, support for Ukraine, and migrant crossings in the English Channel.

events.title: Israeli attacks in West Bank at 'unprecedented' level, PNI leader Barghouti says
events.summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the secretary general of the Palestinian National Initiative (PNI) party Mustafa Barghouti said the level of Israeli attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank had become "totally unprecedented". With tensions escalating, activists accuse settlers of operating with total impunity. "Their goal is clear: it is ethnic cleansing," Barghouti stated, calling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's reaction to the attacks hypocritical.

events.title: Ceuta crisis: ‘No evidence Morocco behind border surge’
events.summary: There is no evidence Morocco was behind the mass influx of migrants that overwhelmed the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July, Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez told lawmakers Thursday. Sanchez's comments followed a police report that emerged this week saying that the mass entry into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration event but a planned and phased operation designed to overwhelm border controls.

events.title: France recorded 'hottest summer ever' in 2026, environment minister says

events.title: About 80 dead in migrant boat tragedy

events.title: Current El Nino extreme weather phenomenon will be 'exceptional', say forecasters

events.summary: A Maltese businessman accused of being the mastermind of the 2017 car bomb killing of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia has been acquitted.

events.summary: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been at a near-standstill for weeks amid the Iran war, sending prices of oil and other key goods soaring.

events.title: Search for survivors from deadly Nepal floods enters eighth day
events.summary: The search for survivors from the deadly floods in Nepal enters its eighth day as mourners have begun to hold symbolic cremations, with morgues overwhelmed by a large number of unidentified remains. The incident claimed more than 1,200 lives and left more than 4,000 missing. NBC News' Daniele Hamamdjian reports on the ongoing rescue efforts and burial ceremonies.

events.title: In Havana, church meals become a lifeline for many
events.summary: As the food shortage in Cuba worsens and some elderly residents look through the trash for their next meal, church volunteers provide what’s become some people’s only meal.

events.title: U.S. strikes targets in Iran near Strait of Hormuz as Iran says it is retaliating
events.summary: President Trump said that the U.S. launched “large and powerful” strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command said that it had targeted “Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran.”  In response, Iran’s armed forces general staff said that it would retaliate. NBC News' Keir Simmons reports.

events.title: Thai police crackdown on sex workers ahead of USS Lincoln’s arrival
events.summary: Police in Pattaya, Thailand, are intensifying a crackdown on sex workers ahead of the arrival of the USS Lincoln after the aircraft carrier’s lengthy deployment in the Middle East. While prostitution is illegal in Thailand, sex workers often operate openly in major tourist hubs like Bangkok and Pattaya.

events.title: Inside the U.K.’s lifesaving treatment for postpartum psychosis
events.summary: Sofii Lewis believes that had she not received treatment within the U.K.’s trailblazing maternal mental healthcare system after being diagnosed with “tendencies of postpartum psychosis,” both she and Evie might not be alive today.

events.title: Nepal flood deaths pass 1,100 as hope fades in the search for survivors
events.summary: The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in this Nepali town devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.

events.title: Thousands of U.S. service members arrive in Thailand after record stint at sea
events.summary: About 5,000 U.S. sailors and Marines are stopping in the resort city of Pattaya for a “rest and relaxation” break as they return home from a record-setting deployment in the Middle East.

events.title: Allies bristle as sanctioned Russian finance minister attends U.S.-hosted G20 summit
events.summary: Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was left out of the “family photo” of finance ministers at a G20 meeting after complaints from Ukraine’s allies.

events.title: Record baby boom brings world’s heaviest parrot back from the brink
events.summary: A record 90 chicks have been added to the population count of the kakapo parrot in New Zealand, delighting conservationists.

events.title: Thieves steal royal necklace from Vienna museum in smash-and-grab heist
events.summary: The robbers, who didn’t disguise their faces and were caught on camera, remain at large with the 673-diamond necklace once owned by an Egyptian queen, police said.

events.title: Death toll in Nepal floods tops 900; number of missing nearly doubles to more than 4,200
events.summary: Rescuers continue to struggle to reach communities days after the massive flooding that stemmed from a glacier collapse.

events.title: Bootleg ‘Spider-Man’ swings into Russian cinemas despite Hollywood boycott
events.summary: While screening the movie “violates both Russian and international law,” everyone, including Russian authorities, “turns a blind eye to it,” one film critic told NBC News.

events.title: Sen. Ted Cruz calls for elections in Venezuela to proceed ‘rapidly’
events.summary: The Texas Republican also said the U.S. should arm protesters in Iran.

events.title: Fears of more flooding in Nepal, 100 Americans among the missing as rescue efforts step up
events.summary: Nepal’s Flood Alert system warned heavy rain could raise water levels in some areas, prompting fresh alerts for residents along waterways.

events.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to more than 700 as nearly 2,500 remain missing
events.summary: The death toll from catastrophic flash floods and mudslides in Nepal rose to at least 734 on Saturday, as nearly 2,500 people remained missing in the country, including about 100 Americans.

events.title: Palestinian woman and NBC News team attacked by masked Israeli settlers in West Bank
events.summary: The woman and the crew were treated for injuries. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence committed “by a handful of rioters.”

events.title: Trump says U.S. has struck deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves
events.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that the U.S. had entered into an agreement with Venezuela to take control of the country’s 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.

events.title: Families wait in agony as Nepal floods leave hundreds missing
events.summary: A New York couple traveling to Mount Kailash is among 65 Americans missing after a catastrophic flood along the Nepal-Tibet border.
